#schema: # Fixture route table for the preflight liveness eval. It is NOT a copy of
# scripts/lib/tool-routes.tsv, and it must not become one: the four helper
# scripts beside it are symlinks into the real tree precisely so the fixture
# cannot drift from the code under test, and this file is the one deliberate
# exception. It exists to make the fixture host-independent.
# The declaration reader rejects any field-one value absent from this column,
# so an unsatisfiable declaration needs a routed tool name that cannot exist.
# Naming a real tool instead -- koto, or shirabe -- would make the eval pass
# or fail on whether the runner happened to have it installed, which is the
# opposite of what a liveness assertion needs.
#   preflight-absent-tool   a name no host ships. Its only route is excluded,
#                           so the absent block ends in the no-route
#                           enumeration rather than an install command a
#                           reader might actually run.
#   sh                      the satisfied twin. Present on every POSIX host,
#                           always at an absolute path outside the working
#                           directory, so the twin resolves without depending
#                           on the runner. Its route is excluded for the same
#                           reason: it is unreachable by construction.
# Both citations name this fixture rather than an issue. The route-table
# schema requires a non-dash citation on any excluded route, and pointing a
# fixture at a real issue number would put a false trail in front of whoever
# reads the enumeration in a report.
preflight-absent-tool
sh
